headline: High: shared project-directory writes and permissive shell/network defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict risks; no direct sandboxing is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and shell; agent_b reads/writes the project directory and has no self-isolation by default. That shared file-based bridge makes prompt injection plausible when agent_a emits content that agent_b later parses as instructions. The pairwise pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF agent_a writes instruction-like content into files or MCP outputs that agent_b later consumes
IF both agents operate on the same project directory without a provenance filter
mitigations: Add a strict content separator for machine-readable outputs
Require agent_b to treat file contents as untrusted data
Disable MCP handoff between the agents for shared artifacts
Review any generated prompt files before agent_b reads them

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches repository metadata, task prompts, and secrets-handling for Ed25519 signatures; agent_b reads and writes the project directory and sends context to a configured model. In a shared workspace, agent_b can ingest files containing agent_a outputs or sensitive prompts, creating a realistic leakage path in default project-directory workflows.
conditions: IF agent_a stores prompts, metadata, or signatures in the shared project directory
IF agent_b uploads those files or their contents to its model backend
mitigations: Move secrets and prompts out of the shared project directory
Restrict agent_b to a scrubbed input subset
Rotate any exposed Ed25519 material if it was written to disk
Add a pre-upload redaction step for agent_b
Use separate workspaces per agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can modify git state and spawn subprocesses; agent_b can write the filesystem, run subprocesses, and supports multiple instances with shared state via the project directory. Both therefore have overlapping write authority on the same mutable workspace, and agent_b lacks git-write capability only partially reducing conflict. This is a default-dangerous coordination problem.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or project directory
IF agent_a performs git operations while agent_b writes files concurrently
mitigations: Serialize access to the project directory
Assign one agent read-only access during the other's write phase
Use separate git worktrees or clones
Add file-locking around writes and commits
Pause one agent before the other mutates state

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces outputs through hooks/workers and MCP, while agent_b is a code generator that writes files then offers to run them. If agent_b treats agent_a's outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into generated code or execution. The profiles show the pathway, but not an explicit verification barrier.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-generated plans, prompts, or code without validation
IF agent_b executes generated code after incorporating agent_a output
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution
Require schema validation on agent_a outputs
Have agent_b cite and cross-check source files before acting
Disable auto-run of generated code
Log provenance for every handoff

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles repository metadata, learning patterns, performance metrics, and task prompts; agent_b handles generated source code and project-directory files. The profiles do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is evident: shared handling of potentially sensitive prompts and code with different retention/handling expectations.
conditions: IF the shared project directory contains regulated or confidential prompts
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two agents' storage paths
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Set a common retention policy for project files
Delete transient prompts after each run
